answer.policy_title: Evolent Clinical Guideline 1759 for Cervical Spine Surgery (part of the '2026 Evolent Clinical Guidelines for Medical Necessity Review – Musculoskeletal Surgery Guidelines')
answer.effective_date: Guideline effective period July 1, 2026 – July 1, 2027 (Original Date: July 2008; Last Revised Date: December 2025; Implementation Date: July 2026)
criteria_quotes: Anterior Cervical Discectomy with Fusion (ACDF) - Single Level. When one of the two following criteria are met: Positive clinical findings of myelopathy with evidence of progressive neurologic deficits consistent with spinal cord compression - immediate surgical evaluation is indicated... OR Progressive neurological deficit (motor deficit, bowel or bladder dysfunction) with evidence of spinal cord or nerve root compression on MRI or CT imaging - immediate surgical evaluation is indicated.

When ALL of the following criteria are met: Cervical radiculopathy or myelopathy from ruptured disc, spondylosis, spinal instability, or deformity; Failure of conservative treatment for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months (defined as lack of meaningful improvement, progression/worsening of symptoms during treatment, or documented medical inability to participate — office/therapy closures, inconvenience, or unexplained noncompliance do not qualify); Imaging studies confirm the presence of spinal cord or spinal nerve root compression (disc herniation or foraminal stenosis) at the level corresponding with the clinical findings (MRI preferred; CT with/without myelography if MRI contraindicated or bony detail needed).

As first-line treatment without conservative care in specific cases (myelopathy/progressive deficit as above; significant cord/nerve root compression due to tumor, infection, or trauma; fracture or instability meeting defined radiographic thresholds — e.g., sagittal angulation >11° at a single interspace or >3.5mm anterior subluxation with radicular/cord dysfunction; C1 atlantodental interval subluxation >3mm in an adult).

Not recommended: In asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic cases of cervical spinal stenosis; In cases of neck pain alone, without neurological deficits, and no evidence of significant spinal nerve root or cord compression on MRI or CT (see separate Cervical Fusion for Treatment of Axial Neck Pain criteria).
answer.appeal_deadline: 180 calendar days from the date of the denial notice (2026-08-14), i.e., by 2027-02-10, per both the denial letter and Magnolia Health's own appeal form instructions.
answer.submission_route: Mail or fax a completed 'Grievance, Appeal, Concern or Recommendation Form' (or an equivalent letter) — or the Prior Authorization Appeal Form — to: Magnolia Health Appeal Department, 111 East Capitol Street, Suite 500, Jackson, MS 39201. Phone 1-877-687-1187 (TDD/TTY 1-877-941-9235); Fax 1-855-300-2614 for appeals (use 1-855-300-2613 only for grievances/complaints, not appeals). Include the reference/tracking number from the denial letter (POC-AAA1CF805A-66883).
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: The Ambetter from Magnolia Health musculoskeletal (spine, hip, knee, shoulder) surgery program is administered by National Imaging Associates (NIA), now part of Evolent Health. The applicable clinical guideline is Evolent Clinical Guideline 1759 for Cervical Spine Surgery, published within Evolent's annual 'Musculoskeletal Surgery Guidelines' document, publicly posted on www.RadMD.com. Providers/members can also call NIA/Evolent at 1-800-424-4912 or log into RadMD.com to view the exact guideline version applied to a specific determination, and Magnolia Health's Medical Management department can confirm which specific version/date of the guideline was used for this particular review.
answer.confidence: high that Evolent/NIA Clinical Guideline 1759 for Cervical Spine Surgery is the governing medical-necessity document Ambetter from Magnolia Health applies to CPT 22551 (confirmed via Ambetter/Magnolia Health's own MSK Quick Reference Guide naming NIA/Evolent as the reviewer for cervical spine surgery, and via Evolent's publicly posted guideline document covering ACDF). Moderate confidence on the exact guideline version (year/date) actually applied to this specific August 2026 denial, since Evolent updates this guideline annually and the payer's internal system may have used a slightly earlier or later revision than the July 2026–2027 version retrieved.
answer.notes: CPT 22551 (single-level ACDF) is explicitly listed in Ambetter from Magnolia Health's Spine Surgery Utilization Review Matrix as a code managed by NIA/Evolent. The denial letter's stated reason ('imaging findings submitted do not support medical necessity') maps most directly to the guideline's 'ALL of the following criteria' pathway, which requires imaging that confirms spinal cord or nerve root compression at the level corresponding to the clinical findings, plus documented failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative treatment within the prior 6 months and a correlating clinical diagnosis (radiculopathy/myelopathy). To appeal, the treating provider should submit updated or annotated imaging reports (MRI/CT) explicitly identifying the compressive pathology at the operative level, correlating clinical exam findings, and documentation of the conservative treatment trial and its failure. The appeal deadline stated in the denial letter (180 days, due 2027-02-10) matches Magnolia Health's own published member appeal deadline for Ambetter (Exchange) members.

Spine Surgery STATEMENT Operative treatment is indicated only when the natural history of surgically treated lesions is better than the natural history for non-operatively treated lesions. All operative interventions must be based on a positive correlation with clinical findings, the natural history of the disease, the clinical course, and diagnostic tests or imaging results. All individuals being considered for surgical intervention should receive a comprehensive neuromusculoskeletal examination to identify pain generators that may either respond to non-surgical techniques or may be refractory to surgical intervention. General Information It is an expectation that all patients receive care/services from a licensed clinician. All appropriate supporting documentation, including recent pertinent office visit notes, laboratory data, and results of any special testing must be provided. If applicable: All prior relevant imaging results and the reason that alternative imaging cannot be performed must be included in the documentation submitted. Purpose This guideline outlines the key surgical treatments and indications for common cervical spinal disorders and is based upon the best available evidence. Spine surgery is a complex area of medicine, and this document breaks out the clinical indications by surgical type. This guideline does not address spinal deformity surgeries or the clinical indications for spinal deformity surgery. Scope Spinal surgeries should be performed only by those with extensive and specialized surgical training (neurosurgery, orthopedic surgery). Choice of surgical approach is based on anatomy, pathology, and the surgeon's experience and preference. Instrumentation, bone formation or grafting materials, including biologics, should be used at the surgeon’s discretion; however, use should be limited to FDA approved indications regarding the specific devices or biologics.
